Subject: Draft: Clarity & Cadence — role responsibilities and comms for upcoming QBR

Team —

Attaching a first-pass comms and a compact responsibility matrix for the April QBR and the operational changes we discussed last month. The goal here is twofold: reduce ambiguity for owners during QBR reviews and give our product/infra squads a clearer escalation path so anomalies are routed consistently.

What's included:
- org-change-slide-deck.pdf — a two-slide summary we can share with the exec QBR packet
- responsibility_matrix.xlsx — role-by-responsibility table (owners, backups, cadence)

Ask: please review for content and tone. Specific asks:
- Laura: can you check the customer-impact wording on slide 2? I want something crisp but not alarmist.
- Vivek: please confirm the escalation & fallback paragraph (bottom of the matrix) matches the operating model you want.
- Karthik: confirm managers list and the proposed reporting line changes are acceptable from a people ops perspective.

Timing: aiming to finalize by EOD Monday (Apr 4) so Communications can prep the all-company note and we can include the slide in the QBR packet.

Attachment notes: both files are lightweight stubs; I've added comments in the spreadsheet on rows 3 and 7.

Thanks —
Neha

Thanks Neha — good, concise start. A few quick notes inline:

> Slide 2 — customer-impact wording

- Suggest rephrase first bullet to: "Short-term support path for regressions: triage → dedicated hotfix → customer notification within SLA window" — less technical in public comms.
- Add a one-line example (high level) about what constitutes a "regression" (drop in P95 latency, serving errors > 0.5%).

On the matrix:
- Row for "Model Rollback" shows Product as owner; suggest adding Engineering Reliability as secondary owner.

I can edit the deck directly unless you prefer comments. Also: for the all-company note, we should include a one-paragraph rationale (why this change now) — I drafted two sentences and attached as redlines.

- Laura

Neha — nice framing. Two operational points to make explicit in the matrix and the comms:

1) Escalation path: add an explicit three-tier path with expected SLAs (owner ack 30m, mitigation plan 2h, exec notification 4h). We have to be very explicit so our CS/Support teams know when to loop execs.
2) Fallback model: if Dedicated capacity is unavailable, we should call out the temporary fallback model (route to hosted variant + rate limit) rather than generic "fallback." That will prevent confusion when a customer asks.

If you want, I can paste a short paragraph for the deck and add a note in the matrix — say if I drop it into slide 2 I think it will read well.

Also: for the all-company email, recommend we schedule a short town hall with Product + Engineering leads the same day the note goes out so we can take 10–15 questions. Communications (cc'd) can advise timing.

— Vivek

SVP, Platform & Reliability

2) Vivek: I'll add the explicit SLA lines to the matrix and call out the hosted fallback plan; please paste the paragraph you mentioned if you have it handy.
